findings.title: Commit bd4b4d0 "Remove temorally the SSO feature" in YunoHost-Apps/sogo_ynh
findings.summary_md: Commit on the YunoHost-Apps sogo_ynh repository authored 2026-07-28T17:52:37Z with the message "Remove temorally the SSO feature". A YunoHost team member later identified this commit in the forum announcement thread as the security patch for the SOGo package vulnerability, and pointed YunoHost 11 users to it as a backport option because the fixed package 5.8.0~ynh9 requires YunoHost 12.1.38 or newer.

findings.title: SOGo: critical vulnerability fixed in 5.8.0~ynh9 (YunoHost forum)
findings.summary_md: Vendor announcement posted by YunoHost developer Josue on 2026-07-29, two months before CVE publication: a critical security issue in the SOGo package is fixed in 5.8.0~ynh9, SSO stays disabled until the package migrates to SOGo 6, and full details were withheld under a roughly one month embargo. It credits Przemyslaw S. Knycz (@djrzulf on GitHub) with the discovery and analysis. In the thread, maintainers state no package fix is planned for YunoHost 11, and affected users describe hand-editing /etc/sogo/sogo.conf as a hot-fix; a later reply reminds operators to restart the server after updating.

findings.title: Vulnerabilities in YunoHost-Apps sogo_yhn software (CERT Polska)
findings.summary_md: CERT Polska coordinated disclosure advisory for CVE-2026-74864 and CVE-2026-74865, both CWE-639 authorization bypasses in sogo_yhn, all versions before 5.8.0~ynh9 affected; the page carries a date-only publication stamp with no time of day. It credits Przemysław Knycz from WeKrwi.IT with the responsible report and describes both mechanisms: the x-webobjects-remote-user header trusted without password validation, and SOGoTrustProxyAuthentication=YES letting any password pass HTTP Basic auth for an existing username.
